walkthroughs.body_html:
Decision Making to Improve Operational Performance — a core area of A-Level Business Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Decision Making to Improve Operational Performance brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Decision Making to Improve Operational Performance.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Modigliani and Miller's irrelevance theorem was published in:

options: Annual cost calculation
Cost of capital
Capital ceiling
Credit cycle

mcqs.q: What do McGregor's Theory X and Theory Y describe?
options: Theory X is about working in a factory and Theory Y is about office work.
Two contrasting management assumptions: Theory X assumes workers dislike work and need control; Theory Y assumes workers can be self-motivated and seek responsibility.
Theory X and Theory Y are stages of business growth.
Share prices are set by the government each morning.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a stakeholder and a shareholder?
options: Stakeholders and shareholders are different spellings of the same word.
A shareholder owns shares in the company; a stakeholder is anyone affected by or with interest in the business — employees, customers, suppliers, community, plus shareholders.
Stakeholders are managers and shareholders are workers.
Share prices are set by the government each morning.

mcqs.q: Why does a company's share price change?
options: Share prices are set by the government each morning.
Share prices reflect investors' expectations about future profits — driven by company performance, sector trends, economic conditions, and market sentiment.
Theory X and Theory Y are stages of business growth.
Share prices go up when a company makes more money this year.
